medSchoolStudLife.diversity: As a global teaching and learning community with more than 116 countries represented, Nova Southeastern University is proud to maintain a campus environment that is genuinely respectful of every human experience and open to the diversity of voices that make up our multicultural community. As a minority-majority university, diversity and inclusiveness are fundamental to how we work together and how we enrich our learning, research and clinical practice environments. The philosophy guides all practices in class, coursework, and professional and collegial relationships, as well as proactive efforts to improve research, education, and patient care efforts to best serve our diverse communities. We are committed to educating our students in a manner that is respectful of all cultural traditions and practices, gender identities, sexual orientations, age, religious/spiritual beliefs, and in all areas that distinguish individuals.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Our first several classes will play a key role establishing a student government, honor code and student organizations that will enrich your student life experience and help you develop as a future physician leader.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
There’s no better location for dedicated medical students than our spacious 314-acre campus in Fort Lauderdale/Davie, Florida, just minutes from downtown Fort Lauderdale. 

See why millions move here: you’ll find year-round sun and outdoors fun, vibrant cuisine and culture. Picture sunny skies and an average temp of 77°. It’s an easy-breezy ride aboard the Shark Shuttle to the beach. Plenty of dining, shopping and entertainment nearby. That’s the place NSU MD calls home!

-Natural beauty: blue-wave beaches, quiet backcountry eco waterways, lush green spaces
-Year-round outdoors fun: kayaking, paddle boarding, biking, fishing, snorkeling, diving, boating, even mountain biking trails
-Sophisticated urban vibe: downtown Fort Lauderdale is minutes away, with renowned cuisine, culture, art, entertainment and shopping
-Central location: NSU is close to the airport, major highways and port. It’s easy to travel to the next city, state − or across the globe
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
On- and off-campus housing services have been established by Nova Southeastern University to provide incoming students, current students, and faculty/staff with an informational resource to assist in identifying options for rental housing near your desired NSU site location.

We provide rental listings including apartments, condos, townhouses, homes, and rooms in private homes.

Other resources include a roommate finder service, moving tips, and frequently asked questions to help make your move easier.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Belonging, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Advisory Council, advances the mission of Nova Southeastern University by cultivating and supporting the ongoing development and implementation of processes, procedures, and programs that promote greater belonging, equity, diversity, and inclusion throughout all aspects of the University so that all members of NSU can be empowered to pursue their full potential and do their very best work.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The NSU Center for Student Counseling Services and Well Being by Henderson Behavioral Health (CSCW) offers student counseling services to the student body of Nova Southeastern University to help them maximize their best self academically, personally and professionally. NSU’s clinical partner is Henderson Behavioral Health, a leader in behavioral healthcare providing comprehensive, recovery-focused services and is accredited at the highest level for Student Counseling Services by the Commission on the Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF).

NSU MD Office of Admissions and Student Affairs (OASA) engages students in wellness events throughout the academic year including, but not limited to, pet therapy, field day, yoga and meditation, and miniature golf excursions. OASA developed the Wellness Committee which is comprised of faculty and students with the objective to enhance the educational experience for students and to provide resources aimed at maintaining and improving their health and wellness.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: We believe that each member of our uniquely diverse NSU community deserves respect and an experience that merges the distinctiveness of the individual with the power of a university committed to fostering excellence, learning, and growth. Your perspectives, your talents, your history, and your voice are critical to sustaining a campus that celebrates difference and fosters respect for all—a place where you belong.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Business casual. Flip flops, sandals, tee shirts with graphics, sweat shirts, sun dresses, tank tops, jeans, denim skirts and spandex are not permitted.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Students are assigned an advisor that proactively addresses problems and serves as a resource to discuss concerns related to your career as a medical student, such as matching and elective selections.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Spending more time learning directly from experienced academic and community physicians provides you with a better understanding of medicine specialties and real-world challenges and opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Our graduates will train to become active learners, work in smaller groups, (7-9 students per cohort), and learn to solve medical problems through active inquiry, under faculty facilitator direction.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Year 3 and 4 clinical clerkships occur in HCA/East Florida Division clinical sites and are scheduled as one-month or two-month discipline-specific clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Accepted students are notified if a prematriculation program is required.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures are optional and will be recorded. Any activity in which there is shared work and an expectation of group participation is required.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Ready for a real challenge? NSU MD is different from any other medical school program. You’ll learn the science of medicine – but we don’t stop there. Through our hybrid, case- and problem-based learning curriculum, you’ll master critical thinking; build your diagnosis and detective skills; and interact with patients as the center of every case.

The NSU MD curriculum was developed by a team of 100 medical educators, physicians and researchers with decades of field experience. As compared to passive, lecture-style teaching, the college’s curriculum is designed to prepare you to interact with patients and health care team members more effectively. 

The innovative curriculum integrates didactics on ethics and humanities, genomics, inter-professional collaboration, biomedical informatics, and leadership, with heavy emphasis on research, technology and innovation.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: An important priority at NSU MD is pairing you with clinical leaders to ensure you receive significant hands-on practice throughout the program. Spending more time learning directly from experienced academic and community physicians, rather than in a classroom, provides you with a better understanding of medicine specialties and sub-specialties, as well as the real-world challenges and opportunities within each.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Approximately $87 million in externally provided funding
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: We are committed to aligning our work with ongoing health care initiatives and promoting synergy among our collaborators that strengthen our mission, and ultimately establish a healthy ecosystem.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Being on the forefront of new discoveries that benefit patients is of the utmost importance. At NSU MD, you will be required to participate in research that will shape your understanding of medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: HCA East Florida, a teaching and research hospital integrated with NSU’s research centers and clinical trial programs. Also, Nemours Children’s Hospital in Orlando, FL offering expert pediatric care.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Demographic shifts, shortages, and cost reductions are changing medicine and our national healthcare system. There’s only one way to prepare future physicians to navigate these challenges: adopt innovative approaches to medical education.

At Nova Southeastern University's Dr. Kiran C. Patel College of Allopathic Medicine (NSU MD), we have redefined medical education. Our innovative approach places the patient at the center of the learning process, using real-world cases and problems as a major vehicle for learning.

NSU MD offers small team-learning, personal mentoring, a large, diverse metropolis, and award-winning hospitals and specialty practices. Each day, NSU MD students tackle complex cases in tight-knit teams. Learn to think critically, diagnose effectively, and treat patients as the center of every case. 

Welcome to a different kind of medical school where you can become a medical provider who makes an impact every day.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Our mission at Nova Southeastern University's Dr. Kiran C. Patel College of Allopathic Medicine (NSU MD) is to advance human health through innovation in medical education, research, patient care, and community engagement. We will achieve our mission with an approach centered on the patient, the student, and the community.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege:
Nova Southeastern University's Dual Admission program in Allopathic Medicine will prepare you for a medical career focused on patients, teamwork, and problem-solving. Dual admission allows you to save a spot in NSU's prestigious Doctor of Allopathic Medicine program while you earn your bachelor's degree, so you can prepare for your future from your first day as an undergraduate student.

With a focus on educating capable diagnosticians, our allopathic medicine program could be the first step on your journey to joining one of the most innovative healthcare professions in the country. Combining cutting-edge technology and scientific discovery with a systems-based approach to collaborative learning, this program, the first of its kind in Florida, creates doctors dedicated to advancing human health.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
Dual Admission undergraduate requirements are for first-time in college students applying to earn a bachelor’s degree. However, college credits earned through advanced high school program may apply. This program is only available to US citizens and US permanent residents (green card holders).

Graduate Admission Requirements are the standards students need to maintain, while earning their undergraduate degree, to remain eligible for the graduate or professional program. For students eligible for the 2+4 accelerated track, it is required that you have earned 30 college credits accepted by NSU, including college-level chemistry and mathematics, before you enter the program. For students eligible for the 3+4 accelerated track, it is required that you enter with college-level science credits, specifically in chemistry, before you enter the program. Students without transferable chemistry credits will be placed in the traditional 4+4 track.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Prior to April 30th, 14 calendar days for response. After April 30th, 5 business days for response.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants must submit a minimum of three and no more than four letters of recommendation. There are no specific requirements regarding the types of letters submitted.

It is recommended that at least one letter be written by a professor who taught you in a core science course and can speak meaningfully to both your academic readiness and your personal suitability for the study and practice of medicine. It is also recommended that at least one letter be written by a clinician with whom you worked during your clinical experiences.

The remaining letter(s) may come from a range of individuals who can provide substantive insight into your qualifications and character, including professors, advisers, clinical research coordinators or preceptors, supervisors, coaches, mentors, and professional colleagues.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Nova Southeastern University's Dr. Kiran C. Patel College of Allopathic Medicine (NSU MD) seeks applicants whose competencies and accomplishments extend well beyond academic achievement. Our Admissions Committee employs a holistic review process to select a class that advances the College’s mission and values. NSU MD does not discriminate against, or grant preferential treatment to, any individual or group on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin.

In evaluating each applicant, the Committee considers all relevant information, including, but not limited to, academic, personal, experiential, and demographic factors. Attributes and experiences of particular importance include:
- A clear and well-articulated motivation to pursue the study and practice of medicine.
- Intellectual curiosity and a demonstrated commitment to addressing complex challenges.
- Evidence of teamwork, collaboration, and the capacity to both support and lead others.
- A genuine commitment to patient-centered care, reflected in personal qualities such as compassion, altruism, and attentiveness to the needs of others.
- Strong communication skills, professionalism, and maturity.
- A solid foundation in the sciences and a record of academic achievement.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours to be eligible for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: NSU MD only accepts continued letters of interest from waitlist candidates.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
All applicants are selected for admission on the basis of their academic, personal, and extracurricular attributes, as well as the intellectual, physical, and emotional capabilities to meet the requirements of our curriculum and of a successful medical career.

Applicants are required to attest at time of acceptance and annually thereafter that they meet these Technical Standards. However, they are not intended to deter any student who might be able to complete the requirements of the curriculum with reasonable accommodations.

Requests from applicants for reasonable accommodations in meeting the Technical Standards will be reviewed and considered by the NSU Office of Student Disability Services.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) administers federal, state and university financial aid programs such as grants, loans, scholarships, and veteran’s benefits. The OSFA provides counseling and assistance to both prospective and current students, including personal budgeting and debt management. A student must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov to be considered for financial assistance. The NSU school code for the FAFSA is 001509.

The student’s Cost of Attendance (COA) budget represents your estimated total cost to attend NSU MD for one year. This amount includes tuition, fees, learning technologies, books, supplies, and a reasonable living allowance. The living allowance is based on the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics and factors in housing, transportation, and personal expenses. These costs may vary depending on the need of the student. For the most updated COA information, please visit https://md.nova.edu/admissions/cost.html

medSchoolPrograms.info:
MD/Oral and Maxillofacial surgery – The MD/OMFS is a six (6)-year combined MD degree and OMFS certificate program. Candidates need to complete their Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS) degree and then match into a residency program that runs concurrently with the NSU MD program.

PhD/MD - This special program consists of a PhD degree followed consecutively by an MD degree. It is not a combined or concurrent dual-degree program. Rather, students complete the PhD program first and, upon successful completion, matriculate into the NSU MD program through a deferred admission pathway. Applications to both the PhD and MD programs are submitted separately and determined prior to matriculation of this special program. For additional information, please contact Robert Smith, PhD, at (rsmith@nova.edu).

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The following premedical courses are required: 
- Biology: 2 semesters (or equivalent) with lab 
- Biochemistry: 1 semester (with or without lab)
- General Chemistry: 2 semesters (or equivalent) with lab
- Organic Chemistry: 2 semesters (or equivalent) with lab 
- Physics: 2 semesters (or equivalent) (with or without lab)
- Mathematics (college level): 1 semester (or equivalent). Calculus is not required. Statistics is acceptable 
- Advanced Placement (AP) courses will fulfill the prerequisite requirements if the individual courses and credits awarded are detailed on the applicant’s college/university transcript 

Upper level core science courses are recommended. The following courses are strongly recommended, but are not limited to:
- Anatomy
- Genetics
- Immunology
- Physiology 
- Virology
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: July 2021. If prerequisite courses are older, then postbaccalaureate or graduate courses in a science or health discipline may be completed within 6 years prior to the year of matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: You must have earned a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in the United States by July 15th of the year you will begin medical school. Your degree may be in the discipline of your choice, as long as you have completed the prerequisite coursework. Academic requirements for admission to NSU MD include adequate preparation in mathematics, biology, biochemistry, chemistry, organic chemistry, and, physics.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
NSU MD Admissions Committee does not require physician shadowing. Applicants are expected to engage in meaningful experiences that demonstrate preparation for the study and practice of medicine, including both medically and non-medically related activities.

For medically related experiences, applicants should show substantive exposure to clinical settings through both direct and non-direct roles. Direct clinical experiences involve observing or supporting patient–physician interactions and may include positions such as caregiver, case manager, emergency dispatcher, paramedic, medical scribe, shadowing participant, or medical assistant.

There is no minimum hour requirement. The Admissions Committee does not assign specific weights to particular activities; instead, applicants are encouraged to present experiences that are meaningful and reflective of their readiness for a career in medicine.
